questions.q: The Bahay na Bato is often described as a 'geometric evolution' of the Bahay Kubo. Which structural principle did it retain from its indigenous predecessor?
o: A completely windowless ground floor for defense
The post-and-lintel framework with a raised living area
The use of 'halipan' rat guards on the stone pillars
The use of heavy limestone for the second-floor walls
questions.n: Despite the stone skirt, the house still relies on a wooden skeleton where the main living quarters are elevated.

questions.q: What is the name of the overhanging balcony or gallery on the second floor that allows air to circulate while protecting the interior from direct sunlight?
o: Zaguan
Caida
Volada
Azotea
questions.n: The volada is a cantilevered walkway that surrounds the living quarters, acting as an air buffer.

questions.q: Which material was most commonly used in the sliding window panels of the Bahay na Bato to admit light while maintaining privacy and diffusing glare?
o: Clear plate glass
Capiz shells
Woven bamboo (sawali)
Stained glass
questions.n: Translucent Placuna placenta shells were framed in wooden grids to allow soft, natural light into the house.

questions.q: The 'Zaguan' on the ground floor served many functions. Which of these was its primary architectural purpose in an urban setting?
o: As the master bedroom (Cuarto)
For parking carriages and storing ritual floats (carrozas)
As the private chapel for the family
As the main family dining hall
questions.n: The zaguan acted as a transitional space between the street and the private home, accommodating large transport.

questions.q: In the vertical organization of a Bahay na Bato, what is the 'Entresuelo'?
o: The stone foundation below the ground
A mezzanine floor used as an office or storage for valuables
The decorative ceiling of the main hall
The highest point of the roof ridge
questions.n: This 'middle floor' was tucked between the ground and second floors, often used by the owner for business.

questions.q: What are the 'Ventanillas' located directly below the large window sills used for?
o: Exits for domestic pets
Allowing air to circulate at floor level while maintaining safety
Purely as decorative wooden carvings
Hidden storage for jewelry and coins
questions.n: These small sliding panels with balustrades allowed cool air to enter even when the main windows were closed.

questions.q: The 'Azotea' is a distinct feature of the Bahay na Bato. Which room is it usually adjacent to?
o: The Master Bedroom (Cuarto)
The Entrance Hall (Zaguan)
The Kitchen (Cocina)
The Grand Staircase (Escalera)
questions.n: It served as an extension of the kitchen for chores like laundry, drying fish, or water storage in jars.

questions.q: What is the name of the landing at the top of the grand staircase where guests were traditionally received before entering the main hall?
o: Comedor
Aljibe
Antesala / Caida
Dispensa
questions.n: This spacious foyer served as a waiting area and a transition into the more formal 'Sala'.

questions.q: The 'Aljibe' was a critical infrastructure component of the Bahay na Bato. What was its function?
o: An underground cistern for collecting rainwater
A reinforced room for protection against intruders
A tunnel leading to the nearest church
A ventilation shaft for the kitchen
questions.n: Located below the azotea or zaguan, it stored water for bathing and cleaning.

questions.q: The 'Sala' is the most formal room in the house. Where is it typically positioned in relation to the street?
o: Directly above the kitchen
On the ground floor for easy access
At the very back of the house for privacy
Facing the main street or plaza to showcase the family's status
questions.n: The sala was the 'showcase' room, positioned at the front to overlook the street life and festivities.

questions.q: Which architectural feature refers to the translucent, wooden-framed window transoms located above the main windows, often filled with capiz or stained glass?
o: Persiana
Espejo
Ventanilla
Callado
questions.n: These 'mirrors' or transoms allow light to penetrate deeper into the high-ceilinged rooms even when the main windows are closed.

questions.q: In the structural layout of a Bahay na Bato, what is the primary function of the 'Callado'?
o: To allow cross-ventilation between interior rooms while maintaining a visual boundary
To act as a reinforcement for the stone walls against earthquakes
To support the weight of the heavy tile roof
To serve as a drainage system for the Azotea
questions.n: These openwork carvings above walls allow hot air to move freely throughout the second floor.

questions.q: Which room served as the formal dining area, usually featuring a long table and a 'punkah' (manual ceiling fan)?
o: Cocina
Comedor
Dispensa
Antesala
questions.n: This spacious room was dedicated to meals and was often one of the most ventilated areas of the house.

questions.q: What is the name of the heavy wooden pillars that extend from the ground foundation all the way up to support the roof, independent of the stone walls?
o: Sillar
Pilastra
Haligue
Kustoriya
questions.n: These internal posts allow the wooden upper floor to sway during earthquakes without being crushed by the stone 'skirt'.

questions.q: The 'Oratorio' is a specialized room found in the homes of wealthy families. What was its purpose?
o: A guest bedroom for visiting priests
A room for musical performances and dancing
A private family chapel for prayer and housing religious icons
A study room for the children of the house
questions.n: Reflecting the deep Catholicism of the era, families had dedicated spaces for their 'santos'.

questions.q: In the kitchen area, what is the 'Dapugan' or 'Kalan' area typically made of in a Bahay na Bato?
o: A hole in the floor for an open fire
An iron cast stove imported from Europe
A portable bamboo tray
A raised stone or brick platform with wood-fired stoves
questions.n: To prevent fire, the cooking area used masonry even if the rest of the second floor was wood.

questions.q: What is the 'Cuarto' in the context of the Piso Principal?
o: The storage for carriage wheels
The kitchen courtyard
The servants' quarters
The bedroom or private chamber
questions.n: These were usually arranged along the perimeter of the house to access windows for ventilation.

questions.q: Which of these describes the 'Escalera' of a grand Bahay na Bato?
o: A drawbridge-style set of stairs
A wide, grand wooden staircase with ornate balustrades and a 'descanso' (landing)
A narrow bamboo ladder at the back
A spiral stone staircase hidden inside a tower
questions.n: The staircase was a status symbol, designed to impress guests as they transitioned from the zaguan to the caida.

questions.q: What was the 'Baño' usually like in a traditional Bahay na Bato?
o: A communal fountain in the Zaguan
A room with a large stone 'tinaja' (water jar) for dipping and pouring water
A separate building in the garden
A shower system using gravity-fed bamboo pipes
questions.n: Before modern plumbing, bathing involved manually pouring water from these large ceramic jars.

questions.q: The 'Piso Principal' refers to which part of the house?
o: The second floor where the main living and formal areas are located
The roof deck used for watching the sunset
The ground floor where the stones are laid
The attic space used for drying grain
questions.n: The 'principal' floor was elevated for better air, views, and social distinction.

questions.q: The Bahay na Bato is famous for its 'Architecture Mestiza' style. What does this term primarily refer to in the context of its materials?
o: A house built entirely out of imported European marble
Houses that used only bamboo and nipa but in larger sizes
A construction style that used no nails or stone
A mix of native wood construction and Spanish stone masonry
questions.n: The term 'Mestiza' reflects the hybrid nature of combining indigenous wooden frameworks with colonial stone foundations.

questions.q: Which level of the Bahay na Bato was traditionally used for the family's main living, dining, and sleeping quarters?
o: The ground floor (Piso Bajo)
The underground basement
The mezzanine (Entresuelo)
The second floor (Piso Principal)
questions.n: Elevating the living area provided better ventilation, privacy, and protection from ground-level moisture.

questions.q: What was the main reason for using heavy stone walls only on the ground floor while keeping the upper floor made of wood?
o: Because stone was too expensive to use for the whole house
To make the house look like a fortress from the outside
To prevent the second floor from getting too cold
To allow the house to be flexible and survive frequent earthquakes
questions.n: The light wooden upper frame could sway during tremors, while the heavy stone base provided a stable foundation.

questions.q: If you wanted to enjoy a breeze while sitting in the shade outside the main rooms, which open-air terrace would you go to?
o: Comedor
Azotea
Zaguan
Aljibe
questions.n: This flat, open stone terrace at the back of the house provided an outdoor space for various domestic activities.

questions.q: Why were the ceilings of the Bahay na Bato built very high, often reaching 3 to 4 meters?
o: Because the wood beams only came in that length
To show off expensive chandeliers
To allow hot air to rise and keep the living level cool
To accommodate the height of tall Spanish furniture
questions.n: High ceilings facilitate passive cooling by keeping the warmest air well above the heads of the residents.
